prompts.Mus: Use case: precise-object-edit. Completely redraw the fly (MUSCA) from reference image 1. The user finds its body and camera angle unnatural. Image 1 is ONLY a palette/finish reference, NOT a pose reference. Image 2 is a loose constellation placement guide; anatomical credibility takes priority over forcing the body into its exact polygon. Output ONE scientifically recognizable, beautiful HOUSEFLY in a natural flying pose, viewed nearly straight from above, with only a very slight three-quarter view. Landscape aspect 380:300 with generous transparent margins. Correct insect anatomy: one head with two realistic reddish-violet compound eyes, two SHORT aristate antennae, substantial compact dark metallic blue thorax, short rounded segmented abdomen, exactly TWO believable thin translucent wings emerging from opposite sides of the thorax on the SAME flight plane, six slender naturally bent legs rooted in the thorax. Wings must be physically proportionate to body, broad near base and smoothly tapering, with fine grey-lavender natural veins and opalescent membrane; NOT giant gold jewelry leaves, not dragonfly, wasp or bee, no long thick horns, no extra wings, no stretched insect. Head directed upper-left, abdomen lower-right, wings spread upper-right and lower-left. Balanced wing silhouette with convincing attachments and a coherent dorsal camera angle. Keep subtle blue-violet nebula speckles within the glossy body and subtle lavender iridescence in wings, softly polished collectible illustration matching the application; minimize gold on anatomy. Approximate canvas composition on 380x300: head around(90,94), thorax(133,134), abdomen down-right toward(185,209); far wing fans through(201,83) toward(320,60), near wing fans toward(55,226) and(145,245). Natural pose and proportion more important than literal node tracing. No geometric star lines, dots, numbers or labels. True transparent RGBA background, no shadows/background haze outside insect. Full insect entirely inside frame.
prompts.Pyx: Use case: precise-object-edit. Completely redraw PYXIS compass using reference1 only for its purple-blue cosmic palette and antique brass materials. User dislikes strange angle and unrealistic structure. Reference2 is only a placement guide. Create ONE authentic antique brass nautical pocket compass, viewed almost straight down, a clear SINGLE circular compass face with consistent perspective and precise concentric rings, dimensional but restrained case thickness, a clear glass cover and one central pivot with one two-ended magnetic needle. Entire object is one circular brass instrument, no open lid, no duplicate dial, no second compass, no intersecting distorted ellipses. Delicate gold engraved bezel and tiny degree ticks, crisp elegant compass rose printed FLAT beneath the needle. One violet/silver needle over the rose, distinguishable from flat dial markings; no pile of gold swords. Deep indigo/purple starfield inside dial with sparse subtle stars and nebula shimmer; enough contrast to read structure at thumbnail size. Only cardinal letters N E S W allowed, each once at correct quarter positions. Small sensible brass suspension loop at top. Landscape transparent RGBA canvas aspect 380:300, instrument face centered around(188,147), approximately 230px outer diameter on this reference frame, with loop extending to y15 and bottom rim near y270. Canvas origin upper-left; scale coordinates proportionally. All three guide positions(160,46),(200,196),(220,254) should lie on the dial/case silhouette. Keep entire compass within margins, natural almost-front view, not tilted dramatically. No guide lines, glowing connector lines, guide dots or numbers. Real transparent background, no shadow plane or checkerboard.
